Complete Numeric Observations Against an Explicit Registry

Source: R/registered-values.R
CompleteRegisteredValues.Rd

Matches one numeric observation to each caller-supplied composite registry key. The registry defines the entire row universe and its order. No Cartesian product, observed group, eligibility rule or biological absence is inferred. The required absent_value applies only to absent rows, never to observed NA.

Usage

CompleteRegisteredValues(data, registry, keys, value, absent_value)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the selected keys and numeric value column.

registry

Data frame with every expected composite key, in output order. Additional metadata columns retain their values and classes. It must not contain the selected value column or observed, status, absent_value columns.

keys

Nonempty plain character vector of distinct key column names. Key columns must be plain dimensionless nonblank character vectors without NA or the reserved ASCII 28 separator.

value

Plain character scalar naming the value column, distinct from keys and reserved output names. Values must be plain integer/double vectors, finite or NA. Complex, classed, dimensional, infinite and NaN values fail. Names on numeric vectors are permitted.

absent_value

Required plain integer/double scalar, finite or NA_real_. No default is supplied. Choosing zero explicitly does not impute observed NA.

Value

A data frame with registry columns, the selected value (double), observed (logical), status (character), and absent_value (double policy). Status is OBSERVED for known matched values, OBSERVED_MISSING for matched NA, ABSENT_FILLED for absent rows with finite fill, or ABSENT_UNAVAILABLE for absent rows with NA fill. Row count and order equal the registry. Empty registry requires empty data and returns a typed empty result. Provenance distinguishes observed zero, filled zero, observed NA and absent NA.

Details

Both tables require unique composite keys. Unknown data keys fail rather than being discarded. Registry metadata is authoritative and carried unchanged; extra data columns are ignored. Inputs are not mutated. Values are normalized to double; no arithmetic or aggregation is performed.

Examples

d <- data.frame(bin = c("a", "b"), fraction = c(0.5, NA_real_))
expected <- data.frame(bin = c("a", "b", "c"), sample = "one")
CompleteRegisteredValues(d, expected, "bin", "fraction", absent_value = 0)
#>   bin sample fraction observed           status absent_value
#> 1   a    one      0.5     TRUE         OBSERVED            0
#> 2   b    one       NA     TRUE OBSERVED_MISSING            0
#> 3   c    one      0.0    FALSE    ABSENT_FILLED            0
